questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Define inflation as a sustained rise in the general price level
questions.stem: A transit planner notes that bus fares rose 3% this quarter while the overall consumer price index rose 5%; this is best described as

options.text: inflation because the general price level rose
a rise in relative prices only, not inflation
options.misconception: confuses relative price change with general price level change

options.text: deflation since only one price rose
options.misconception: mistakes a single price move for the aggregate index
labels any price rise as stagflation

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level, not a single relative price. The 5% CPI rise signals inflation even though one fare rose less.
questions.hint: Look at the overall index, not one fare.

questions.stem: A transit planner's board records a nominal interest rate of 8% and expected inflation of 3%; apply the Fisher equation to find the real interest rate
questions.explanation: The Fisher equation gives real rate approximately nominal minus inflation, so 8% minus 3% equals 5%. The exact form yields a slightly lower value but 5% is the standard approximation.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Describe money demand collapse in hyperinflation
questions.stem: Explain why money demand collapses during hyperinflation in a transit system context

answer.exemplar: When prices rise rapidly, holding cash erodes purchasing power, so households and firms minimize cash balances and spend immediately, collapsing real money demand.

questions.explanation: Rapid inflation destroys the store-of-value function of money, so agents hold minimal cash. Real balances fall as velocity rises.
